figures.label: S11
figures.caption: Figure S11. XRD patterns of the precipitate after adding MnCl2 to a 0.1 m Li2S solution. Note. To minimize the influence of air oxidation and uncontrolled hydrolysis during the precipitation experiment, the Li2S solution was prepared using N2-purged deionized water, and the whole precipitation process was carried out in an Ar-filled glove box. MnCl2 powder was directly added into the 0.1 m Li2S solution, and the precipitate was collected and dried under protected conditions before XRD characterization. The obtained XRD pattern can be mainly indexed to MnS, with almost no obvious diffraction peaks from other crystalline phases. These results indicate that MnS is the dominant crystalline precipitate under the strictly controlled experimental conditions, supporting the Mn2+-induced trapping of soluble sulfide species.
